paper.title: Bias of the occurrence probability in iETS odds-ratio and inverse-odds-ratio models, and a score-based occurrence error proxy

definitions.definition: Inverse odds ratio occurrence model (SB23, eq. 18): o_t ~ Bernoulli(p_t), p_t = 1/(1+mu_b,t), mu_b,t = l_b,t-1, l_b,t = l_b,t-1 (1 + alpha_b e_b,t) (multiplicative error) or log l_b,t = log l_b,t-1 + alpha_b e_b,t (additive error); in smooth: occurrence='inverse-odds-ratio' (C++ case 'i' in src/headers/ssOccurrence.h).

Odds ratio occurrence model (SB23, eq. 16): p_t = mu_a,t/(mu_a,t+1), mu_a,t = l_a,t-1, l_a,t = l_a,t-1 (1 + alpha_a e_a,t) (multiplicative error) or log l_a,t = log l_a,t-1 + alpha_a e_a,t (additive error); in smooth: occurrence='odds-ratio' (C++ case 'o').

The proxy for the unobservable occurrence error that smooth uses (occurrenceError() in src/headers/ssOccurrence.h): v_t = o_t - p_hat_t, u_t = (1 + v_t)/2; iETS_O: 1 + e_a,t = u_t/(1-u_t) = (1+v_t)/(1-v_t); iETS_I: 1 + e_b,t = (1-u_t)/u_t. With an additive occurrence error the log of the same ratio is used.

The recursion that produces the one-step-ahead probability $\hat p_t$ from the occurrences $o_1, \dots, o_{t-1}$, the initial state and the smoothing parameter $\alpha$: $\hat p_t = f(\mu_{t-1})$ with $f(\mu) = \mu/(1+\mu)$ for [[D2:iETS_O]] and $f(\mu) = 1/(1+\mu)$ for [[D1:iETS_I]]; the state is updated on every observation through an error proxy $e_t$ computed from $o_t$ and $\hat p_t$, as $\mu_t = \mu_{t-1}(1 + \alpha e_t)$ (conventional multiplicative error), $\log\mu_t = \log\mu_{t-1} + \alpha e_t$ (additive error) or $\mu_t = \mu_{t-1}(1 + e_t)^{\alpha}$ ([[D16:ADAM multiplicative ETS update]]).
Croston (1972): SES on demand intervals q and sizes z, updated only at demand occurrences; probability forecast 1/q_hat.
Long-run mean of p_hat_t produced by an occurrence filter applied to o_t ~ Bernoulli(p) with constant p, after a burn-in; compared with the true p.
Simulated o_t, independent Bernoulli(p) draws with p fixed over time.

Proxy proposed in this study: the score of the Bernoulli occurrence log-likelihood o log p + (1-o) log(1-p) with respect to the log of the state, at p_hat_t: e_a,t = o_t - p_hat_t (mu_a: iETS_O, iETS_G) and e_b,t = p_hat_t - o_t (mu_b: iETS_I, iETS_G). Additive error: log mu_t = log mu_t-1 + alpha e_t (a score-driven filter with unit scaling); multiplicative error: mu_t = mu_t-1 (1 + alpha e_t). Derivation: derivations.md section 4.

For an [[D4:occurrence filter]] applied to $o_t \sim \text{Bernoulli}(p)$, a value $x^*$ of the one-step-ahead probability at which the expected update of the state is zero: $h(x^*) = 0$ with $h(x) = E[e_t \mid \hat p_t = x]$ (additive error) or $h(x) = E[\log(1 + e_t) \mid \hat p_t = x]$ (ADAM multiplicative error); for the conventional multiplicative update the expected change of the state is $\alpha\mu_{t-1}h(x)$. It is stable when $h$ moves $\hat p_t$ towards $x^*$ on both sides.

Observation-driven time series models whose time-varying parameter is updated by a scaled score of the conditional log-likelihood (generalised autoregressive score / dynamic conditional score models).

Recursions theta_t = theta_t-1 + alpha H(theta_t-1, o_t) with fixed gain alpha; as alpha tends to 0 their iterates concentrate around the stable zeros of the mean dynamics d theta/dt = E[H(theta, o)] (the ODE method).
The upward bias of Croston's 1/q_hat as an estimate of the occurrence probability, from Jensen's inequality applied to an SES of the demand intervals; of order alpha.

Stationary mean probability minus the true p, for an occurrence filter applied to Bernoulli occurrence with constant probability p; estimated by simulation with a batch-means Monte Carlo standard error.

definitions.term: alpha-to-0 limit of the stationary mean probability
definitions.definition: For a filter and a p, the intercept at alpha = 0 of the least-squares line of the stationary mean probability on alpha, fitted to simulations at small alpha values; compared with the zero-drift point.

definitions.term: random design over p and alpha
definitions.definition: Pairs (p, alpha) drawn at random with a fixed seed: p uniform on [0.02, 0.98] and log(alpha) uniform on [log 0.001, log 1]; or values of p drawn uniformly on [0.02, 0.98], each simulated at a fixed set of small alpha values. Each cell: one simulated series of Bernoulli occurrences, filter started at the true value, burn-in discarded, batch means for the standard error.

The update of a multiplicative level under ets="adam" in smooth: mu_t = mu_t-1 (1 + e_t)^alpha, i.e. log mu_t = log mu_t-1 + alpha log(1 + e_t) (adamGvalue() in src/headers/adamGeneral.h, case MNN); conventional ETS uses mu_t = mu_t-1 (1 + alpha e_t).

Proxy proposed in this study for a multiplicative occurrence error under the [[D16:ADAM multiplicative ETS update]]: $1 + e_t = \exp(s_t)$, with $s_t = o_t - \hat p_t$ for $\mu_a$ ([[D2:iETS_O]]) and $s_t = \hat p_t - o_t$ for $\mu_b$ ([[D1:iETS_I]]), so that $\log\mu_t = \log\mu_{t-1} + \alpha s_t$; in smooth proxyOccurrence='score' with ets='adam'.

The [[D8:score proxy]] used with a multiplicative occurrence error in the form $1 + e_t = 1 + s_t$, with $s_t = o_t - \hat p_t$ for $\mu_a$ and $s_t = \hat p_t - o_t$ for $\mu_b$; under the conventional ETS update this gives $\mu_t = \mu_{t-1}(1 + \alpha s_t)$ (in smooth proxyOccurrence='score' with ets='conventional'), under the ADAM update $\mu_t = \mu_{t-1}(1 + s_t)^{\alpha}$.
The 3,000 pre-registered M5 series (subset.csv, seed 20261029): daily unit sales, days 1-1,969, leading zeros removed, the last 14 days held out (SB23 section 5).

adam(y, "MNN", occurrence=X, distribution="dgamma") in smooth (ADAM in Python), with occurrence X in fixed (F), direct (D), odds-ratio (O), inverse-odds-ratio (I), general (G) or auto (A, selected by AICc among the others); O, I, G and A each with proxyOccurrence "ratio" and "score", under ets="conventional" and ets="adam"; F and D once, conventional (the proxy does not change them): 18 methods named iETS_<X>_<proxy>_<conv|adam>.
Syntetos-Boylan approximation of Croston's method: Croston's forecast times (1 - alpha_q/2); tsintermittent::crost(type="sba") with default settings.
Teunter-Syntetos-Babai method (SB23 eq. 6), tsintermittent::tsb() with default settings; point forecasts only.
Hurdle shifted Poisson filter, counter::hsp() (counter 0.3.0.41003 from github.com/config-i1/counter), with upper quantiles from side="upper" at each level.
Negative binomial filter, counter::negbin(), with upper quantiles from side="upper" at each level.
Root mean squared scaled error of M5: sqrt(mean over h=1-14 of (y - f)^2 / mean over the in-sample of (y_t - y_t-1)^2), per series.
Scaled cumulative error: sum over h=1-14 of (y - f), divided by the in-sample mean; negative values mean over-forecasting.
Scaled absolute periods in stock: |sum over j of sum over i<=j of (f_i - y_i)| over h=1-14, divided by the in-sample mean.

Mean over h=1-14 of the pinball loss of the upper quantile at level tau (0.80, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99), divided by the in-sample mean absolute first difference; also computed for the quantile rounded up (SB23 eq. 35).
Share of the 14 held-out days with y at or below the upper quantile at level tau; also for the quantile rounded up.

Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the per-series differences, score proxy minus old proxy, zero differences dropped (scipy.stats.wilcoxon, zero_method='wilcox'), with Holm's correction over the comparisons of each test at the 1% level; the direction of a difference is the sign of the median non-zero difference.

Multiple comparisons with the best (Nemenyi test on ranks) by rmcb() of the Python greybox at the 99% level: mean ranks of the methods over series, with intervals; two methods differ statistically significantly when their intervals do not overlap.
Per series and method, the sum of the 14 point forecasts of the held-out days; the score proxy minus the ratio proxy gives the direction in which the proxy shifts the forecast.
The upper quantile of an iETS forecast at level tau rounded up to the next integer, ceil(q_tau), so that it is a value the count data can take (Svetunkov and Boylan 2023, eq. 35).

Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the per-series differences in scaled pinball, rounded-up quantile minus raw quantile, of the same iETS method and level; zero differences dropped (scipy.stats.wilcoxon, zero_method='wilcox'); Holm's correction over the 72 tests (18 iETS methods x 4 levels); the direction is the sign of the median non-zero difference.

Per iETS method and level tau: |mean over series of the coverage - tau|; compared rounded minus raw as D, with a 10,000-draw percentile bootstrap interval over series (seed 20261030) at level 1 - 0.01/72 (Bonferroni over the 72 method-level pairs).

Proposed, not implemented: the score proxy scaled by the inverse Fisher information of the Bernoulli log-odds, s_t = (o_t - p_hat_t)/(p_hat_t (1 - p_hat_t)), used in place of o_t - p_hat_t for mu_a (and its negative for mu_b), with the same conventional and ADAM ETS forms as the score proxy (1 + alpha s, and exp(s) - 1 under ets='adam'). E[s_t] = 0 at p_hat_t = p for any positive scaling, so the zero-drift property of the score proxy holds; after a long run of zeros (p_hat small, o_t = 1) s_t is about 1/p_hat, close to the reactivity of the ratio proxy. Scaled scores of this kind are the inverse-information scaling of score-driven (GAS) models (Creal, Koopman and Lucas 2013).

warrants.text: C12 shows the stationary mean of Croston's 1/q_hat converging to p as alpha tends to 0, and C1 shows that of iETS_I and iETS_O with the old error proxy converging to a zero-drift point different from p; the two biases therefore differ in kind: one vanishes with the smoothing parameter, the other does not.

By C10 the old proxy pushes the probability of iETS_O up and that of iETS_I down. iETS_G updates mu_a as iETS_O does and mu_b as iETS_I does, and its probability is mu_a/(mu_a+mu_b), so the two upward pushes on its states act on the probability in opposite directions. The M5 RMSSE of iETS_G under conventional ETS changed little with the score proxy (C21: not significant at the 1% level), unlike that of iETS_O and iETS_I. iETS_A selects among the iETS models by information criterion and inherits the same offset.

By C5 the old proxy biases the probability of iETS_I under conventional ETS downwards, and on M5 the forecast sum of iETS_I rises when the score proxy replaces it (C20). A lower probability puts more mass at zero and lowers the upper quantiles. At 0.99 the lower quantiles of the old proxy gave a lower scaled pinball on most series and a better MCB rank, while their mean scaled pinball was higher and their coverage further below 0.99 (table T1 of E23).

After a demand that follows a run of zeros, with a small one-step-ahead probability p_hat, the old proxy of iETS_O gives 1 + e_a = (2 - p_hat)/p_hat, a jump in the state of about 2/p_hat, close to Croston's interval update; the score proxy moves the log of the state by o - p_hat, at most 1 (C11). A filter that reacts strongly after long runs of zeros adapts faster to changes in the probability, which may be worth more on non-stationary retail series than the removal of the bias; the RMSSE gains of the score proxy were large only where the old proxy's bias was large (C21).

NegBin and HSP rank better than every iETS model on the scaled pinball at 0.80, 0.90 and 0.95 whichever proxy the iETS model uses (C24, C22), and rounding the iETS quantiles up does not close the gap (C25, C26). The iETS models model demand sizes with a continuous Gamma distribution, NegBin and HSP with count distributions; the occurrence proxy changes the probability, not the shape of the size distribution.

open_questions.question: Whether the score proxy scaled by the inverse Fisher information of the Bernoulli log-odds, (o - p_hat)/(p_hat (1 - p_hat)), keeps the zero drift of the score proxy and the reactivity of the old proxy, and so improves the accuracy of iETS models, is not established.
How much of the bias of the old error proxy the likelihood estimation of the occurrence smoothing parameter and initial level absorbs on real data is not established.
